**Surat al-Anfal**

It is also called *al-Jihad* (striving in the way of Allah). (*Bismillah*) meaning: the One to whom belong all power, might and strength. (*al-Rahman*) the One who encompassed the circle of reason with the suns of proofs from every transmitted source. (*al-Rahim*) the One who bestowed favour upon whomever He wills of His followers.

The purpose of this surah is the disavowal of strength and power by the servants, and their exhortation to submit to the command of Allah, which produces the unity of the word, which produces the victory of the religion and the humbling of the corrupters, which yields every good. What unites all of this is that, since it was established in the earlier surahs that it is obligatory to follow the command of God and to unite upon it, because of what has been established of His uniqueness and His power, the aim of this surah is to make obligatory the following of the one who calls to Him, with complete submission, acceptance and contentment, and the disavowal of all strength and power in favour of the One who bestows these, and who, if He willed, could take them away. The clearest evidence for this in it is the story of the spoils (*anfal*), over which they disagreed and disputed their division. Allah prevented them from it, restrained them from the desires of the self, and obliged them to humility and modesty. He gave them to His Prophet (ﷺ), because it was he who defeated them by the pebbles he threw, through which Allah broke the customary order by scattering them into the eyes of all of them, and by the troops He sent down. It was as though the matter belonged to him alone, granting it to whomever He wills. Then, when it came into the possession of the Prophet (ﷺ), (p-215) he returned it to them as a favour from him to them and a kindness towards them.

Its name is *al-Jihad* likewise, because the disbelievers are always many times the Muslims, and no group of the people of Islam has ever fought except against more than themselves; and enduring against a superior number is obligatory. Had the consideration been to other than His power, glory be to Him, that would not have been bearable. For these aims, its recitation was established in jihad, to rouse the believers to combat, even if the hosts and numbers of the enemies multiply, and the companies of reinforcements from all the servants come to them one after another. This was mentioned by the memorizer (*al-Hafiz*) Abu al-Rabi' Sulayman ibn Musa ibn Salim al-Kala'i al-Maghribi in *Futuh al-Bilad* from his book *al-Ikتifa fi Sirat al-Mustafa wa Ashabihi al-Thalatha al-Khulafa*; and likewise his teacher, the preacher (*al-Khatib*) Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Hubaysh, in his book which he compiled on the conquests. Both said, concerning the battle of al-Yarmuk in the conquests of al-Sham, on the authority of the narration of Sayf ibn Umar, and this is the wording of Ibn Salim: He said: The reciter on that day was al-Miqdad. They said: Among the sunnah which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established after Badr was that we recite the surah of jihad at the time of encounter, and it is Surat al-Anfal. The people continued upon that afterwards. Both said, concerning the battle of al-Qadisiyya in the conquests of Persia, and the wording is also that of Ibn Salim: They said: When Sa'd, that is Ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, prayed the noon prayer, he ordered a boy whom Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, had assigned to him, and who was one of the reciters, to recite the surah of jihad. All the Muslims at that time were learning it, and he recited it over the company next to him, and it was recited in every company, so the hearts of the people were gladdened and they recognized tranquility (*sakina*) through its recitation. Mus'ab ibn Sa'id said: Its recitation was a sunnah which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would recite at the time of the clash (*zukhruf*), and he would have it recited; so the people acted upon that. End.

Its connection to al-A'raf is that when He, exalted is He, mentioned, as has preceded, the stories of the Prophets, peace be upon them, with their peoples in that surah, it was fitting to mention the story of this noble Prophet (ﷺ) with his people. And it has preceded that when He, glory be to Him, elaborated on the story of Musa, peace be upon him, that might have given the impression of his superiority over all; so He brought the story of the one addressed by this Qur'an in two complete surahs: al-Anfal at the beginning of his affair and during it, and Bara'a (al-Tawba) at the close of his affair and its conclusion. He distinguished between the two stories. That is because the people of Musa, peace be upon him, were in severe torment, and they knew from their forefathers that Allah would remember them and deliver them from the hands of the Copts. When Musa, peace be upon him, came to them and made clear to them the signs which Allah had commanded him with, they did not doubt that he was the one promised to them as the mercy of Allah towards them, and his coming was a benefit to them, immediate, along with the benefit to come. So they unanimously followed him. They were more than six hundred thousand fighting men, yet despite that they would oppose him at every little thing, and they did not find hearts with which to confront the Copts in refusing to comply with their commands. As for Muhammad (ﷺ), he came to his people with no sense of prophethood among them and no knowledge of it, and they were not under the humiliation of anyone; rather they were the kings of the Arabs. So they thought that he had come to strip them of their honour and make them his followers, and so they opposed him in the strongest opposition, and left no scheme untried until they engaged him in turning him back from what he had brought. Despite that, Allah granted him victory over them, and He continued to support him until people, both they and others, entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, and He made His religion prevail over every religion, as He, glory be to Him, had promised. Then He strengthened his affair after him, and his followers have never ceased to be dominant, and they will not cease until the Day of Religion. (p-217) Between the two stories there is a distinction for those of insight and mastery. As for the connection of the beginning of this surah to the end of that one: it has become clear that the end of al-A'raf is the end of the story of Musa, peace be upon him, concluded with the story of Bal'am, and that what follows it is but completions of what preceded, which are necessary, and completions of the completions, until the last of that was the praise of those whom He qualified for His presence, glory be to Him, with submission and complete humility. When they were attached to that exalted presence, this required a question about the condition of those who are with the one addressed (ﷺ), and so it was answered

with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you﴾, meaning: those who are with your Lord are the ones who in reality defeated the disbelievers, as you have known, and it will come with its explanation. So they are the ones deserving the spoils (*anfal*), and they have no inclination toward them; their concern is only worship. As for those with you, I made them merely an outward instrument. Yet, despite that, they ask ﴿about the spoils﴾ which I have entrusted to them through the hands of My soldiers, asking in a manner of dispute, from which one should seek refuge in Allah, as He has warned at the end of al-A'raf, because that leads to the division of the word and weakness in resisting the enemies. *Anfal* is the plural of *nafl* (with a vowel on the first letter), which is what is given to a warrior in addition to his share; and what is meant here is the spoils (*ghanima*), which is the property taken from the people of war by force. It was named that here because its original meaning in the language is excess, and the Muslims have been favoured by it over the rest of the nations.

When the question was about its ruling, it was as though it had been said: "So what is to be done?" He said, indicating that they had asked about its disposal and ruling, so that the answer would match the question: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to them, in answer to their question: ﴿The spoils belong to Allah﴾, that is, the One from whom alone victory comes, because of what He has of the attributes of perfection, ﴿and the Messenger﴾, that is, the one who was resolute in the command of Allah, submitting to His decree, proceeding in what He sent him with, not fearing the contact of destruction through meeting the enemy. Abu Hayyan said: There is no disagreement that the verse was revealed concerning the day of Badr and its spoils. Ibn Zayd said: There is no abrogation (*naskh*) here; He merely informed that the spoils belong to Allah in that they are His possession and His provision, and to the Messenger, peace be upon him, in that he is the explainer of the ruling of Allah and the one who proclaims it by His command, so that submission may occur from the people; and the ruling on the division came down in the midst of that. End.

When He, glory be to Him, informed that they have no share in them except by the command of Allah and His Messenger, and that this necessitated that they halt until His command, glory be to Him, was made manifest through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ); and since piety necessitates standing still out of fear until the proof comes which one is emboldened to follow, He consequently said: ﴿So fear Allah﴾, that is: be in great awe of Him in all your states, of the One for whom there is no greatness but His and to whom no command belongs but His. So do not seek anything without the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and do not dispute with one another; for Allah, exalted is He, who showed you mercy by sending a Messenger for your deliverance and sending down a Book for your protection, is not one who neglects what would set you right. He will give you what His knowledge has decreed to be yours, and withhold from you what is not yours.

﴿And set right the state of affairs among you﴾, that is, the condition which is the very cause of your separation and union. For the most prominent aspect of it is the clear one which is severance, and it has come close to corruption through each party seeking preference over its companion. So turn to tending to it by submitting to the command of Allah and His Messenger, who command you to turn away from the world, so that He may divide it among you equally; the strong and the weak are equal. For you are provided for and victorious only through your weak ones, so that your word may be united, your affair be strengthened, your support be firm, and you be able to establish the religion and suppress the corrupters. ﴿And obey Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom all greatness belongs, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, that is, the one whose greatness is from His greatness, in everything they command you, such as giving extra shares to whomever he sees fit, carrying out conditions, and fulfilling covenants with those with whom he has made them.

When He had commanded and forbidden, He stirred and inflamed, and so He said, explaining that faith necessitates obedience: ﴿If you are believers﴾, that is, truthful in the claim of faith. For not everyone who claims something is truthful in his claim until he demonstrates it through testing. For this reason He connected to it His saying, emphasising with the utmost emphasis, because being freed from worldly concerns is difficult.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 8, verse 2:

﴿Only the believers are﴾ that is: those firmly established in the attribute of faith, ﴿who﴾ that is: who establish the proof for their claim of faith by making their deeds confirm their words, so they become ﴿those who, when Allah is mentioned﴾ that is: the One who combines the attributes of perfection, of majesty and of beauty, merely by being mentioned, as in His saying: ﴿The spoils belong to Allah﴾ [al-Anfal: 1], ﴿their hearts tremble﴾ that is: they are seized by a great fear that penetrates the marrow of their bones and circulates through all their inner meanings and bodies, ﴿their hearts﴾ that is: (p-220) merely at His mention, out of magnifying Him. ﴿And when His verses are recited﴾ that is: read in continuous succession and sequence by whoever reads them, ﴿to them﴾ that is: as occurs in establishing the proofs for that ruling mentioned therein, ﴿they increase them in faith﴾ that is: through their belief in them and through what is obtained for them of the light of the heart and the tranquility of certainty by means of them; for they are what indicate Allah through what they make clear of His magnificent acts and the descriptions of His majesty and beauty. The manifestation of proofs is stronger for what they point to. The complete power of Allah the Exalted is only known through the traces of His wisdom in His creatures, and that is a sea without shore. Since the levels have no end, the levels of manifestation and knowledge have no end; so the increase is in the persons of assent. ﴿And upon﴾ that is: while they are ﴿their Lord﴾ that is: the One constantly beneficent to them, alone, ﴿they rely﴾ that is: they continually renew the ascription of their affairs to Him, however much Satan whispers to them about poverty or otherwise, so that He may suffice them from where they do not reckon, for His treasuries are vast and His hand is ever-pouring, night and day. Just as, when they relied upon Him in battle, He gave them victory, though they were in the utmost fear of being forsaken, and their condition was fitting for that given their anxiety, their fear, their being killed and their weakness.

When He described them with faith, which drives them to obedience and reliance on Allah and gathers them together and repels whatever would hinder them from it, He moved from the works of the heart to the works of the body, making clear that their resolve lies only in worship and noble conduct: ﴿who establish prayer﴾, meaning they never slacken in renewing it. Since prayer is a link between the creature and the Creator, He followed it with the link between creatures (p-221): ﴿and from what We have provided them they spend﴾, meaning in keeping with Our greatness, and it is Ours rather than theirs, ﴿spend﴾ even when they are of modest means, relying on what is with Us. So spending and disdaining the world are their resolve, not greed for it. Thus they are like those who are ﴿with your Lord﴾ in adorning themselves with worship and emptying themselves of the world through turning away from it and asceticism. This is a reminder of the description of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun, those who are mindful of Allah) mentioned at the beginning of the Book in His words: ﴿Those who believe in the unseen, and establish prayer, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾ [al-Baqarah: 3].

Al-Biqa'i, *Nazm al-Durar*, on surah 8, verse 4:

When they verified their faith (*iman*) through the deeds of the heart, the limbs, and wealth, and thereby fulfilled all the branches of the religion, God, glorified is He, magnified their station by His saying: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the people of lofty resolve, ﴿they﴾, that is, exclusively, ﴿are the believers﴾. He emphasized the content of the sentence with His saying: ﴿truly﴾.

Since their five mentioned attributes, which comprise moral qualities and actions, have effects in purifying the hearts and illuminating them with divine knowledge, and since the stronger the influence, the higher the effects, and since these attributes are degrees, their reward is likewise. Therefore God, exalted is He, said, in answer to one who might be understood to ask, "What is their reward for this?": ﴿For them are degrees﴾. And since He multiplied them by using the sound plural, in accordance with what the context of favour indicates, He magnified them with His saying: ﴿with their Lord﴾, that is, through their submission to His command.

Since the decree of God is great, and since man is weak and insignificant in reaching what is incumbent upon him in this regard, and since he is prone to self-admiration even at the slightest of his deeds, He, glorified is He, indicated that he cannot but rely on pardon, even if he exerts himself beyond his effort, so He said: (p-222) ﴿and forgiveness﴾, that is, for their sins, if they turn back from disputing over the spoils (*al-Anfal*) and other matters.

﴿and a generous provision﴾, that is, there is no constriction in it nor any turbidity in any way, from disputing or otherwise. He will make them independent of these spoils and fill their hands with wealth from the booty of Persia, Byzantium, and other things. This is in this world, but as for the Hereafter, it is beyond what description can encompass. Abu Hayyan said: "Since three inward attributes preceded, namely fear (*wajal*), the increase of faith, and reliance upon God, and bodily and financial ones, three things followed from them. The inward deeds were matched with degrees, the bodily with forgiveness, and the financial with a generous provision. This type of correspondence is one of the finest examples of the science of *badi'*." End of quotation.

Since faith, according to al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, is belief, affirmation, and action, he permitted the saying: "I am a believer, God willing (*in sha' Allah*)", because the fulfilment of the actions is doubtful, even though belief and affirmation are certain. According to Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, faith is only belief and affirmation, so he did not permit the exception (*istithna'*). The disagreement is therefore verbal. This applies when the exception is made out of doubt. If it is made for another reason, it serves to break the self's boasting, to bear witness to the Paradise that belongs to the believer, and to pass judgement on the state at the time of death. Moreover, this expression does not contradict certainty; it is merely a matter of seeking blessing, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, God willing, secure﴾ [al-Fath: 27]. Imam Fakhr al-Din mentioned this.

When leaving behind worldly gain was hard on the soul, and abandoning dispute after having been bound to it was even harder, he began to mention to them what they had disliked, and he did it to them and commanded them to it, knowing its outcomes. So they praised its effect, so that it would be more conducive to their submission to his command and their restraint through his rebuke [p-223]. He likened their dislike of giving up their own desire in the spoils (al-Anfal) to their dislike of going out with him, and then to their dislike of meeting the army rather than the caravan (al-'Ir). Then they saw the best outcome in both matters. So he said: ﴿As﴾, that is: their state in disliking the surrender of the spoils, although surrender was the truth and better for them, was as their state was when ﴿your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth﴾, that is, the One who is good to you by guiding you to all the aims of goodness, ﴿from your house in truth﴾, that is, the decisive matter that separates the firm from the unsteady. ﴿And indeed﴾, that is, while the state was that ﴿a party﴾ (he expressed it thus because their opinions were tending toward division) ﴿of the believers﴾, that is, those firmly established in faith, ﴿were averse﴾.

Then he mentioned the evidence of their dislike, saying: ﴿They argue with you﴾, meaning: they repeat that, desiring to turn you away from meeting the army, to return from it.

Since the army was a matter that God had decreed, so that it must occur, although it pleased Him, He said: ﴿concerning the truth﴾, meaning: which is the preference for jihad, ﴿after it had become clear﴾, meaning: it became manifest with a great, easy clarity, without the difficulty of reflection, by the indications of circumstances: the caravan's escape, the ease of the matter of the mobilized force, and the Messenger ﷺ informing them, sometimes explicitly and sometimes allusively, as in his saying: "By God, it is as if I am looking at the places where the people will fall; this is the place where so-and-so will fall, and that is the place where so-and-so will fall."

Since He, glorified is He, had decreed the encounter and the victory, as support for His friend and the elevation of His word, despite their intense dislike of that, He likened His driving them toward His purpose [to driving]. (p-224) So he said, using the passive voice, because what was hateful to them was the driving, not who did it: ﴿as though they were being driven﴾, meaning: a driver drives them, and they have no power to resist him, ﴿to death while they are looking on﴾. This was because it was the first raid the Prophet ﷺ undertook in which there was an encounter, and they were not fully prepared for battle; they had only set out to meet the caravan. Moreover, they were few in number, while the number of the people of the mobilized force was great, and they were in extreme awe of meeting them and terror of fighting them. All of this is a reminder to them that none helped them but God, without any effort on their part; rather, they were in the grip of His power like a tool in the hand of one of them, so that this would yield the conclusion that they have no right to dispute concerning the spoils.

When they had softened toward this address and turned to the King, the Ever-Relenting, He turned to them and said: ﴿And [remember] when﴾, meaning: remember what God has mentioned to you, when your state was as He described. Then He led on to a great happiness and a might unlike any other might. And remember when ﴿God promised you﴾, meaning: God, who combines all the attributes of perfection, ﴿one of the two groups﴾, the caravan or the army. He substituted for "one of the two" the clause ﴿that it would be yours﴾, so that the promise concerning it would be repeated. That is, ﴿you disliked encountering the one with the might﴾, ﴿while you wished﴾, meaning: and you were loving with a great love, ﴿that the one without might﴾, meaning: the weapons, the fighting and the combat by which champions are recognised and men are distinguished from women of the tents, ﴿would be yours﴾, meaning: the caravan, because only a few men were in it, said to be forty men. This was your ignorance of the outcomes. Then it became clear to you that what God had done was better for you in a way that its full reality cannot be reached. So submit the matter to Him, in secret and in public, ⁽p-225⁾ and you will attain wealth and victory.

The Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr al-Asimi said, regarding the connection of the sequence of al-A'raf to this surah and the connection of the end of that one to the beginning of this one, the following text:

When He, glory be to Him, related to His Prophet ﷺ in Surat al-A'raf the accounts of the nations, and the believers concluded from the totality of that that guidance comes only through prior happiness, [the surah] opened with mention of the wretched through the story of Iblis and closed with the story of Bal'am. Both of them disbelieved with knowledge, and what they had already attained did not benefit them. God, exalted be He, alerted His servants to the door through which Bal'am was reached, by His saying: ﴿But he inclined to the earth and followed his own desire﴾ [al-A'raf 7:176]. He thus indicated that following desires misguides with every kind of misguidance. They were alerted to what contains prudence, namely abandoning desires altogether, so He said, exalted be He: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ [al-Anfal 8:1], and so on. It had been said to them: leave aside what you see as your own due right, and entrust the matter to God and His Messenger. That is safer for you and more prudent in restraining your aims, suppressing your appetites and abandoning the affairs of your Lord. In this easy, white Sharia, He has established at length the blocking of means (sadd al-dhara'i') and the placing of the likelihood of a thing in the position of the thing itself, such as the prohibition of a sip of wine or a drop, the betrothal during the waiting period, and the heavy sleep being counted as invalidating (wudu'). These are likelihoods on which the ruling was not based for their own sake, nor because of what they are, but because of what they are likelihoods and means toward that which was forbidden for its own sake, or which deserved a ruling for its own cause and specific reason. When the Muslims were ordered to remove their hands from the spoils on the day of Badr, the fighters had resolved to take them and had entertained the notion of keeping them exclusively, and they regarded them as their right, and that whoever had not directly engaged in fighting, such as the elders, or whoever had withdrawn for an important task, had no right to them. The others also regarded their own right to them as established, because they had been a support and a refuge for the fighters behind their backs. God's command to them to refer the ruling in this to God and His Messenger was an instance of blocking the means, because fulfilling their aims in this, though each of the two groups clung to some argument, is a likelihood of leadership over souls and of making the following of desires easy. So God commanded them to refrain from this and to entrust the matter to God and His Messenger, for that is safer for them, more faithful to their religion, more lasting in reconciling their mutual relations, and more beneficial in following. ﴿So fear God and set right what is between you﴾ [al-Anfal 8:1], and so on. Then they were reminded of what they ought to adhere to, and He said, exalted be He: ﴿The believers are only those﴾ [al-Anfal 8:2], up to His saying: ﴿and it increases them in faith﴾ [al-Anfal 8:2]. Then they were alerted that the goods of this world, whether spoils or otherwise, should not be relied upon by the believer in a way that brings upon him harm from associating partners or a turning toward other than God, glory be to Him, through His saying: ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾ [al-Anfal 8:2]. Then they were reminded of what He described of the God-fearing: prayer and spending. Then He said: ﴿Those are the believers in truth﴾ [al-Anfal 8:4], as an alert that whoever falls short in these states and does not bring them to their perfection has not left faith, but descends from the rank of perfection according to his shortcoming. In this there was an indication of their excuse in their speech concerning the spoils, and that they had been, in their seeking, in a state of rightness and had drunk from adherence and following. But the highest ranks are what was made clear to them and granted to them, and that is perfection and success. Then God, glory be to Him, alerted them to the manner of their setting out toward Badr, and their wish that the one without might would be theirs, while He, glory be to Him, was showing them the goodness of the outcome in what He had chosen for them. They had wished to encounter the caravan and had chosen that over encountering the enemy, and they did not know what lay beyond that.

﴿And God desires to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the root of the disbelievers﴾ [al-Anfal 8:7], up to what He related to them of being enveloped by His mercy, the comprehensiveness of His gentleness and His bounties, and the expansion of their souls. He alerted them to what makes their certainty firm and increases their faith. Then He informed them that all good lies in God-consciousness, and so He said: ﴿O you who believe, if you are God-conscious, He will grant you a criterion﴾ [al-Anfal 8:29], the verse. This criterion is what Iblis and Bal'am were deprived of, and so there came from them what preceded of following desires, which cut them off from mercy. The verse included the attainment of the good of this world and the Hereafter through the blessing of God-consciousness. Then both goods were summarised together in His saying: ﴿and God is the possessor of great bounty﴾ [al-Anfal 8:29], after the detail of what the believers hasten toward: the criterion, the expiation and the forgiveness. The good of this world specifically was not stated explicitly, though the verse implied it, out of honouring the believer in the position of granting the criterion, the expiation of misdeeds and forgiveness, and so the mention of the transient enjoyment of this world, which is play and sport, was not made to be detailed alongside what is not of its kind nor similar to it.

﴿And indeed the abode of the Hereafter, that is the true life﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:64]. Then the verses were joined together. Another aspect: when He said: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it﴾ [al-A'raf 7:204], He explained to them the manner of this listening and what the believer is characterised by of its kinds, and so He said: ﴿The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned﴾ [al-Anfal 8:2], the verse. These did not merely hear with their ears, nor were they ears that do not hear with them or hearts that do not understand with them. Had they been like that, they would not tremble, and dread and fear would not overcome them, and the verses would not increase them in faith. Hence the hearing of the believer is only of this kind: ﴿And do not be like those who say, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾ [al-Anfal 8:21]. Since these people were only affected by following their desires and standing with their aims and appetites, ﴿taking the goods of this lower life﴾ [al-A'raf 7:169], and ﴿but he inclined to the earth and followed his own desire﴾ [al-A'raf 7:176], this very thing was the bane of Iblis. He saw for himself more, and believed he had the right to it, and then followed this desire when he said: ﴿I am not one to prostrate to a human whom You created from clay, from black mud moulded﴾ [al-Hijr 15:33]. Since the following of desire is the root of misguidance and of deviating from the straight path, He commanded the believers to close the door of desires, and to submit in matters that have a connection to them, even if they are not pure desire, but are a likelihood of facilitating the following of desire. Thus the surah opened with their question about the spoils, and they were informed that they belong to God and His Messenger, who judges concerning them as He wills.

﴿So fear God﴾ [al-Anfal 8:1], and beware of the desires that destroyed those whose mention was related to you. ﴿And set right what is between you﴾ [al-Anfal 8:1] by removing dispute. Submit to God and His Messenger, or else you will not be hearers. You have been commanded to listen with the listening through which mercy is hoped for, and its explanation is in His saying: ﴿The believers are only﴾ [al-Anfal 8:2], the verses. Another aspect: the narratives of the Children of Israel were followed by the admonition to the believers, especially concerning God-consciousness, according to what generally prevails in what is mentioned about the Children of Israel. In al-Baqarah He followed their narratives with His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not say "Ra'ina," but say "Unzurna" and listen﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:104]. Since their narratives opened with mention of their being preferred — "O Children of Israel, remember My blessing which I bestowed upon you, and that I preferred you over the worlds" — He opened the address to this community with something that alerts to their being preferred. Consider the difference between "O Children of Israel" and "O you who believe." He commanded those to believe: ﴿And believe in what I have sent down﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:41], and He commanded these to a cautious worship, saying: ﴿And say "Unzurna" and listen﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:104]. Then al-Baqarah was followed by Al 'Imran and opened with the explanation of the decisive and the ambiguous, through which He came upon the Children of Israel in many of their transgressions. Since Surat Al 'Imran included mention of them with what occurs in it, it was followed by His saying, exalted be He: ﴿O you who believe, if you obey a group of those who were given the Book, they will return you to disbelief after your faith﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:100]. Then the surah was followed by His saying: ﴿O mankind, be God-conscious of your Lord who created you from one soul﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:1]. He turned away from the address by the name of faith for the sake of connection. That is because Surat Al 'Imran singled out from the transgressions of the Children of Israel crimes such as their saying about the disbelievers: ﴿These are better guided than those who believed, in the way﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:51]; this is slander. Among them is their saying: ﴿God is poor and we are rich﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:181], up to ⁽p-230⁾ what lay between these two of verses indicating their deliberate commission of crimes. So He turned away from "O you who believe" to "O mankind" [al-Nisa' 4:1], so that it would be more fitting in arrangement and clearer in its connection to what was mentioned. When Surat al-Nisa' included His saying: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who judaised, We made unlawful to them good things﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:160], up to His saying: ﴿and their taking of people's wealth falsely﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:161], it was followed by His saying: ﴿O you who believe, fulfil the contracts﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:1]. Then He mentioned to them what was made lawful for them and what was forbidden to them, so that they would beware of what those had fallen into. Accordingly, when Surat al-A'raf included their narratives in summary, and explained in it their transgression, and built it upon the following of desires and the assault upon aims, He sought from these people protection against that and distance from what resembles it in summary. So it was said at the end of the surah: ﴿Indeed, those who are God-conscious, when a passing thought from Satan touches them, remember﴾ [al-A'raf 7:201]. Then the other surah opened by turning them away from what they had a connection to and an attachment to, which would give them a legal excuse for what came from them. So it had been said to them: leaving this is more knowing and further from following desires, so submit in that matter to the ruling of God and His Messenger, and be God-conscious of God. Then the context was woven together and the verses were joined. The connection of al-Anfal to al-A'raf has been made clear in several aspects, and praise belongs to God. End of quotation.

When He, exalted be He, informed of what is true, that their will and even their love were directed only toward the caravan and not toward the army, it became clear that they had no part in what occurred. For had they had a part, it would have been as they wished. So they have no share in the spoils except what God apportions to them, because the judgment belongs to His will, not to the will of anyone else. So He said, exalted be He, conjoining with ﴿and you wish﴾: ﴿and God desires﴾, that is, by what He has of might, majesty and knowledge, ﴿to establish the truth﴾, that is, to make it firm in the world of witnessing what is firm with Him in the unseen world, and this here is the encounter with the one with might, ﴿by His words﴾, that is, those He revealed to His Prophet ﷺ: that they will be defeated, killed and taken captive, and that this is the death-place of so-and-so and this is the death-place of so-and-so, so that He may exalt His religion and manifest His command over every matter. ﴿And cut off the root﴾, that is the last, ﴿of the disbelievers﴾, that is, just as their first is cut off, meaning: He will uproot them so that no one of them remains who opposes his party. He manages your affair as He wills, and therefore He chose for you the one with earnestness and might, so that what He promised you of raising the religion and suppressing the corrupters would come about by cutting off their root.

Surah 8, verse 8 — Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar)

﴿That He may establish the truth﴾, i.e., the one which is His religion, the upright (al-qayyim), and in which lies the success of both abodes; ﴿and nullify falsehood﴾, which is everything that opposes it; ﴿even though the criminals dislike it﴾, i.e., that. ﴿The criminals﴾ are those who sever what God has commanded to be joined, and [He will do this by] breaking their strength through your weakness, annihilating their multitude through your scarcity, and dissolving their might through your humiliation, so that He manifests the supremacy of His command and subdues the necks to His remembrance.

﴿إذْ﴾ is an adverb of time (ẓarf) ﴿لِيُحِقَّ الحَقَّ﴾ [al-Anfal: 8] ﴿تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ﴾ means you were asking your Lord for help, that is, you were seeking the aid of the One who had shown you kindness. It is a substitute (badal, a form of apposition) for ﴿إذْ يَعِدُكُمُ﴾ (when He promised you). It is therefore an explanation (bayan) of their aversion to meeting the one with might (﴿ذاتِ الشَّوْكَةِ﴾), shown by their intense dismay, which made them seek help, while the outcome revealed that the good lay in what they disliked, that He would establish the truth, make the religion manifest, and weaken the affair of the polytheists.

When He hastened the response, He indicated this by His words: ﴿فاسْتَجابَ﴾ (so He answered), meaning He brought about the answer in the manner of one who is himself seeking it and very eager for it, ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ (for you), in full accordance with what you wanted, to strengthen your hearts, ﴿أنِّي﴾ (that I), meaning that I am ﴿مُمِدُّكُمْ﴾ (your supplier), meaning one who brings about reinforcement (المَدَدِ) (p-232) ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ (for you), meaning by supplying you. Perhaps he changed the expression to the explicit pronoun because of the greatness and blessing it carries. ﴿بِألْفٍ مِنَ المَلائِكَةِ﴾ (with a thousand of the angels) while they were ﴿مُرْدِفِينَ﴾ (following), meaning coming after, each followed by their likes.

[p-233] Since the victory of the Muslims in this raid was very evident, He said: ﴿And Allah did not make it﴾, meaning the reinforcement and the promise of it, given the majesty He possesses, such that whoever contemplates it does not stand in awe of anything, ﴿except as good news﴾, meaning so that your souls might be gladdened by it. He did not need to restrict it by saying "for you." As for the story of Uhud, the number of Muslims killed was greater than the number of unbelievers killed, so had He not said "for you," some doubts might have arisen upon hearing the first part of the statement that the reinforcement was good news for the unbelievers.

Since what was judged here regarding the reinforcement was that it was itself good news without restriction, it is understood that concern for it is greater. Therefore, the thing judged was likewise the reassurance. The original wording would thus be: "except as good news, and it is a reassurance." For this reason, it was necessary to place His pronoun in His words "by it" before "the hearts," to emphasize His matter and magnify His standing, and as an indication of its completion, following the habit of the Arabs of placing first what they care about most, which they regard as most important. So He said: ﴿and that your hearts might be reassured﴾, meaning and a reassurance, so that they might be reassured, ﴿by it﴾, meaning by Him alone, without regard to any of your strength or anything else, ﴿your hearts﴾. So this verse is of the type called *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device in which one element is omitted from one clause because it is mentioned in another, and vice versa). As for the story of Uhud, when the good news was restricted to the reinforcement with "for you," for the reason already mentioned, it is understood that the reassurance is likewise restricted. Therefore, the more fitting arrangement was to delay His pronoun and to place first "the hearts" that are connected to their pronoun, to balance His words "for you."

Since this made clear that victory lies in His hand alone, and that no reinforcement or anything else necessarily brings victory by its own nature, He stated this explicitly in His words: ﴿And victory is not﴾, meaning obtained and existing through the angels or other causes, ﴿except from the presence of Allah﴾, meaning because He alone possesses the attributes of perfection. What He has is not confined to the reinforcement by the angels. So victory, even if it comes through them, does not come from them. Therefore, do not rely upon their presence, nor be weakened by their absence, but rely upon Him alone, for what He has of causes cannot be encompassed by knowledge. This applies if He intends victory through causes. If He intends otherwise, He does so. So the expression "from the presence of" (ʿinda) was used to convey this meaning.

Since this raid was at the beginning of the matter, and after the true promise had appeared to them, that they would gain one of the two groups, they were averse to meeting the one that had great might, and then what happened to them of victory occurred, the context required affirming the might and wisdom of Allah by way of emphasis, to inform that the attributes of perfection belong to Him permanently. He grants victory to whoever is patient and God-fearing by His might, and He perfects His command in the most complete manner by His wisdom. This is His practice always, as He did in this raid. Therefore He said, giving the reason for what precedes and emphasizing: ﴿Indeed Allah﴾, meaning the Supreme King, ﴿is Mighty﴾, meaning He is at the utmost degree of invincibility and of subduing whoever wishes to subdue Him, forever and ever. He is not overcome, and His ally is not in need of an increase in numbers or the preciousness of equipment. ﴿Wise﴾, meaning when He decrees a matter, it is in the utmost perfection and firmness, so no one can diminish anything from it. This is His permanent attribute. He acts this way in granting you victory, however much you find comfort in His good news and do not look to your strength or anything else besides Him. So do not be distressed when He commands you to advance into danger, even if it involves meeting all the people.

Since He emphasized it here, He did not need to repeat the emphasis in Al ʿImran, so He said: ﴿the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [Al ʿImran 3:126], meaning the One who informed you of His might and wisdom in the Battle of Badr with what suits that context of emphasis, and informed you that if you ransom the captives, a number equal to them will be killed the following year. The occurrence of the matter as He said suffices without further emphasis. None of the Muslims at Uhud hesitated to engage or feared it, except for what occurred of the intention to show weakness on the part of the two groups, and their protection from it at that moment. More detailed explanation of this has already been given in Al ʿImran.

When He mentioned the good news and the tranquility brought about by the reinforcement, it was fitting to mention that He followed the word with the deed. By His might and wisdom, He cast tranquility, security, and calm into their hearts. The evidence for this is the drowsiness that overcame them in a place that is the furthest thing from it: the place of combat, of fighting rivals, and of staying alert against the treachery of the hostile people. The same applies to the rain and its effect. He said, also as a substitution (badal) from ﴿And when He promised you﴾ [al-Anfal: 7], or as something dependent on the victory, or on what the adverbial phrase contains of the sense of a verb (ramihat al-fi'l), depicting His might and wisdom: ﴿when He covered you with drowsiness﴾. In the reading of Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr, the first letter of the imperfect is vowelled with a fatha, so the subject is "al-nu'as" (drowsiness). The rest read it with a damma on the yā'. Nafi' pronounced the ghayn with a sukun, and the rest with a fatha, and they doubled the kasra-marked shīn. In the first reading, the subject is then an object here, and in the second, the subject is a pronoun referring to God. When He mentioned this strange covering, which breaks habitual patterns, He mentioned the purpose for which it was done, saying: ﴿security﴾. Because this was extraordinary and against custom, the description came with His words ﴿from Him﴾, meaning by His wisdom, since in such a situation no one sleeps except the one who feels safe. He also prevents the enemy from reaching you while you sleep, by His might. The causative verb is not inflected differently among the three readings, because the drowsiness being the subject is figurative (majāz). In my view, it is also valid to read the word in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl).

Since drowsiness is a sign of death, He mentioned after it the sign of life, saying: ﴿and sends down upon you﴾, and He confirmed that it was rain with His words: ﴿water from the sky﴾. In al-Baydawi, and originally in the tafsir of Abu Ḥayyān, it occurs that the polytheists reached the water first and gained control of it. This is not so. Rather, it was the believers who reached Badr first and gained control over its water, as is established in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere. Thus the explanation of the story is that they were rained upon at the station from which they set out toward Badr. So the Muslims obtained from it enough to fill their water containers, and they performed ritual purification from minor and major impurity. It also packed the sand for them and made their march easy, while what fell on the polytheists made their ground slippery until it prevented them from marching. This was a cause for the Muslims to arrive at the station before them, and it enabled them to build the cisterns and to fill in (taghwīr) what lay beyond the water where they had camped, from the low ground, as is well known in the biographies. The "rijz of Satan" (rijz al-shayṭān, his whispering) to them consisted of making them feel few and weak and frightening them with the enemy's numbers. The "binding upon the hearts" is their reassurance. He also comforted their souls with the honour He showed them, as all of this is made clear by the words of Ibn Hisham: ﴿and sends down upon you from the sky﴾, water, for the rain that fell upon them that night. It restrained the polytheists from reaching the water first and left the believers free to reach it. ﴿So that He may purify you thereby﴾, that is, from every filth. He began with purification among the benefits of water because it is closest to the qualities of the angels who are brought near to the presence of holiness. He joined to it, with His words ﴿and remove from you﴾, meaning from you and not from others, ﴿the rijz of Satan﴾, without the lām, that which is necessarily attached to him, namely the servant who is in a state of ritual impurity (ḥadath), of which major impurity (janābah) is a form. It brings one near to satanic impurities, through tightness of the chest, doubt, and fear, to keep the angels away from the presences. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The angels do not enter a house in which there is a junub." The word rijz is applied to filth, to the worship of idols, to punishment, and to polytheism. Satan had indeed whispered to them, and there is no doubt that his whispering is among the greatest filth, for it drags whoever persists with it to all that has been mentioned. Then He joined to it what the heart was prepared to receive of divine wisdoms, which is the pouring out of tranquility, and He said: ﴿and to bind﴾, meaning with patience and certainty.

Since that was a firm, strong, and high binding, He expressed it with the particle of elevation, saying: ﴿upon your hearts﴾, meaning after making them settle into trust in His kindness at every affliction, until they were filled with every good and the binding became fixed in them. He compared them to a sack filled with something and then tied at its mouth so that nothing of what is inside can escape. He repeated the lām to indicate that this is the greatest aim, and what came before it was a means toward it. He joined to it, without a lām, what necessarily accompanies it of firmness, saying: ﴿and to make firm thereby﴾, meaning by the binding through the rain, ﴿the feet﴾, meaning so that there is no fear, for one who is afraid does not keep his foot steady in the place where he stands. Rather, his leg moves involuntarily, or else by the packing of the sand.

When he mentioned the wisdom of the reinforcement and its effects that make hearts and feet firm, he mentioned what the reinforcements were commanded to do, namely to strengthen them through speech and action. So He said: ﴿When﴾, being a third substitute (*badal*, a grammatical apposition) for "when He promised you," or an adverb of time (*zarf*) governing ﴿your Lord revealed﴾, i.e., the One who bestows favor upon you in all of that, ﴿to the angels﴾. He made clear that the victory comes from Him and not from the reinforcement, by His saying: ﴿that I am with you﴾, i.e., whoever I am with will be victorious in all that he hopes for. ﴿So make firm﴾, i.e., by means of that, ﴿those who believe﴾, i.e., with kinds of strengthening: by increasing their numbers, strengthening their hearts, fighting their enemies, making the enemies appear few in their eyes, and belittling their status. Then he explained the "being with" by His saying: ﴿I will cast﴾, i.e., by a promise that admits no breach, ﴿into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾, i.e., those who brought disbelief into being, ﴿terror﴾, so that they will have no steadfastness. ﴿So strike﴾, i.e., O believers, both angels and humans, not fearing because of that. (p. 238)

Since striking the neck and the head is the most deadly means of killing a person, and the neck is usually covered in war, He expressed it by His saying: ﴿above the necks﴾, i.e., the heads, or the upper parts of the necks, because these are joints and places of slaughter.

Since destroying the fingers is the most painful blow after that, as it nullifies the struck person's fighting or its completeness, He said: ﴿and strike from them every fingertip﴾, i.e., there is no obstacle to that, since I am with you.

Then he gave the reason for their being empowered over them, saying: ﴿That﴾, meaning this great empowerment, and he informed of it with: ﴿because they﴾, meaning those who have now become entangled in disbelief, even though some of them would later be granted faith, ﴿opposed God﴾, meaning the Supreme King whose vengeance cannot be withstood, ﴿and His Messenger﴾. That is, they sought, by violating the commands and prohibitions, to be on a side other than the one on which the party of guidance (ḥizb al-hudā) stood, with deception and trickery, and they opposed Him by openly drawing the sword. Then he explained what awaits the doer of this, saying, conjoining it to what was implied: ﴿So whoever opposes God and His Messenger, then [you should do to him what you have done to them], for indeed I will do to him what I did to these.﴾ He made the idgham (assimilation of consonants) apparent in the present-tense verb (yushāqqi) because the story concerns the Arabs, and their enmity after the Hijrah was severe and open. He made it assimilated in the past-tense verb (shāqqū) because what preceded it was a matter between concealed scheming and open subjugation. He used the present tense to encourage repentance, by restricting the threat to continuance. He assimilated in both places in al-Ḥashr (Surah 59) because the story concerns the Jews, whose affair was weak and concealed in scheming: ﴿And whoever opposes God﴾, meaning the One to whom all command belongs, so that no one has any command alongside Him, and opposes Him secretly or openly, ﴿and His Messenger﴾ by being on a side other than the one they are pleased with, ﴿then indeed God﴾, meaning the One who possesses all attributes of perfection, ﴿is severe in punishment﴾. That is, He has this attribute, so let whoever opposes Him expect His punishment. Thus the verse contains iḥtibāk (a rhetorical device in which each part omits what the other mentions): mentioning the assimilated verb first is evidence of the omission of the apparent verb second, and mentioning the apparent verb second is evidence of the omission of the assimilated verb first.

When He concluded the verse by explaining the cause that necessitates the humiliation of those who disbelieved, and by mentioning His great attributes, He followed it with what He says to them, to explain their state at that time, by saying, turning to them (iltifāt) for greater rebuke and reproach:

﴿That﴾ means: He, glorified is He, by virtue of this awe-inspiring attribute of His, makes His enemy taste of His punishment, which they have no power to bear and no strength to withstand. So the tongue of the state (*lisan al-hal*, the eloquence of the situation) addresses them on behalf of speech: "The matter about which the Messengers warned you and the Books brought you, and at which you used to mock, O disbelievers, is this matter whose impact is severe and whose consequence is far-reaching for whoever it descends upon. Its repelling has overtaken you, so why do you not repel it? No indeed, by God, it has occupied everyone who faces it, and he cannot grapple with it."

Since what befell them at the Battle of Badr, of killing, capture and subjugation, was very small compared to what awaits them in the Hereafter, He called it a taste (*dhawq*), because a taste is by a small amount, so that by it the condition of the large amount may be known. So He said: ﴿Taste it﴾, i.e., experience it as subjugation, with the experience of one who tastes it. And know that, compared to what you will face, it is like the taste of something compared to the thing it is a taste of. ﴿And that﴾, i.e., and the matter that the Messengers and Books brought you is that for you, along with this which you have tasted in this world, [there is] ﴿the punishment of the Fire﴾. This was originally the structure, but it was stated openly for generality and to attach it to the attribute, so He said: ﴿for the disbelievers﴾, i.e., on account of their disbelief, even if they do not openly display opposition, ﴿the punishment of the Fire﴾, which is what you will encounter, and it is greater, and you will see.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 8, verse 15:

When he had established their humiliation in this world and the Hereafter, by the fact that He made their hearts regretful, it was fitting that this be followed by a prohibition, addressed to those who claim faith, against fleeing from them, and a threat to whoever turns back from them after this clarification while still claiming faith. So He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, i.e., in what came to them from their Lord, ﴿when you meet those who have disbelieved﴾, i.e., in the signs of their Lord, opposing them, ﴿advancing﴾. He expressed the state of their meeting by the verbal noun (masdar) for the sake of intensifying the comparison, so He said ﴿zahfan﴾, i.e., while they are advancing in battle, and they are so numerous that the movement of their advance, even if swift, cannot be perceived except as a crawling advance (al-zahf). ﴿Then do not turn your backs to them﴾, i.e., fleeing from them, even if you are fewer than them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 8, verse 16:

﴿And whoever turns his back to them﴾ Since the battle usually takes place during the day, and turning one's back is something whose occurrence is not limited by a time frame (because its duration is not extended), disobedience happens merely by a glance taken with the intention of fleeing, while persistence (al-tamadi) means repeating such instances, and there is no condition for the correctness of applying the name, he (Allah) expressed it with "the day" and removed "fi" (in) from it, as a recommendation to return to the attack after fleeing, with no ambiguity. For a time expression is not a measure for an act unless its time is extended, like fasting, so He said: ﴿on that day﴾, i.e., when you encounter them in this state, at whatever time of the battle it may be, by night or by day, ﴿his back﴾, i.e., he makes his back toward them, for any reason, turning away in a manner in which he does not intend to return to the fight from it, ﴿except﴾, i.e., while he is ﴿swerving﴾ (mutaharrifan), or the state is swerving, which is leaving the direction of straightness, ﴿for battle﴾, i.e., which cannot be made easy for him except by that, imagining to his enemy that he is defeated, as a deception against him, and then he charges back against him; ﴿or withdrawing﴾ (mutahayyizan), i.e., moving from one position to another and retreating, ﴿to a company﴾ (fi'a), i.e., another group from among the people of his party, who are fit for him to return to in order to seek their help or to help them.

Since this is the place where the listener anticipates the answer and empties his mind for it, He answered, linking with the particle fa (then), to inform that the act mentioned is the cause of this consequence, so He said: ﴿then he has certainly earned﴾, i.e., returned, ﴿wrath from Allah﴾, i.e., from the One possessing all attributes of perfection, ﴿and his refuge is Hell﴾, i.e., it will frown upon him, just as he feared the frowning of the disbelievers and the meeting of scowling faces with a grim, scowling countenance, ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾. This applies if the disbelievers do not exceed double (their number), as the text will state.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 8, verse 17:

When He had laid down the prohibition concerning that, He gave the reason for it by affirming His might and wisdom, and that victory comes from none but Him. Whoever's faith is sound will not hesitate to comply with His commands. Thus He said, giving as the cause of His prohibition of fleeing, even if the enemy is numerous, a reminder of what He did for them at Badr, so that He would make them act in the same way again, and to prevent them from being pleased with the extraordinary events that took place at their hands on that day: ﴿So you did not kill them﴾, meaning: wrath befalls the one who turns his back, because it became clear to every believer that He, exalted be He, does not command anyone except to do what He is able to enable him to do. For it has become evident, from what occurs according to the established customs, that you did not kill the slain of Badr even though you engaged in the means of killing them, because you did not put into the hearts of that great army the terror which was the cause of their defeat, which in turn was the cause of the killing of those whom you killed, given your weakness in resisting them under normal custom. In this there is also, along with that, a restraint for them from saying, boastfully, "I killed so-and-so and so-and-so men, and I did such-and-such."

﴿But Allah﴾, meaning: the One to whom all command belongs, so nothing falls outside His will, ﴿killed them﴾, meaning: by defeating them for you when they saw the angels, and their eyes were filled with the dust which he ﷺ threw at them, and their hearts were in dismay, until you were able to kill them, a breach of custom which He had promised you, so His word was true and His deeds were fulfilled.

When He returned what they had done to Himself, exalted be He, He followed it with what His Prophet ﷺ did, as a proof of this. For when he ﷺ saw the Quraysh approaching, he said: "O Allah! This is Quraysh, who have come with their arrogance and pride, opposing You and denying Your Messenger." Then Jibril, upon him be peace, said: "Take a handful of dust and throw it at them." He did so, and their eyes were filled, and they fled. (p-243) So He said: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw﴾, meaning: O master of the believers, the sand into the eyes of the disbelievers, ﴿when you threw﴾, meaning: the form of throwing it from your hand was produced; because this effect that resulted from your throwing is beyond custom, it is clear that it was not your action. This is the answer to why He did not say, "So you did not kill them when you killed them," because the departure of the soul from a severely wounded body is the customary course, and they were the ones who killed them when they engaged in striking them. So it is not valid to say, "So you did not kill them until you killed them." What is negated is only the cause that precedes the killing, which makes killing possible, namely the calming of their hearts that arose when they advanced, and the terrifying of the disbelievers that arose from their weakness and defeat, which made them killable. Thus what is negated from them is the initiation, and what is negated from him ﷺ is the ultimate result. Or, when the angels, upon them be peace, engaged in killing some of them, it was valid to negate from them the killing of the group absolutely. Or, when some of them boasted of killing someone, He, exalted be He, negated it from them absolutely, because their engaging in killing those who were killed, in the face of what He had prepared for them of means and supported them with of hosts, is nothing. As for the Prophet ﷺ, he did what he was commanded to do, throwing the sand, and did not repeat his action nor mention it; so He, exalted be He, affirmed it for him while negating its effect from him and affirming it for the One to whom all affairs are returned, as a discipline from Him, exalted be He, for this community, meaning: let no one look upon any of his acts of obedience, for We have negated this great act from the most perfect of creation, while he is knowing and acknowledges that it is from Us. So let the one who sees an action of his own beware of the great severity of Our reprisals. Rather, let him attribute all his good deeds to Allah, exalted be He, just as the throwing was attributed to Him by His saying: ﴿But Allah﴾ (p-244) meaning: the One whose command none can repel, ﴿threw﴾, because He is the One who conveyed its effect with that which defeated the disbelievers. He did all of that in order to test the disbelievers through the hands of whomever He willed of His servants, a trial of evil outcome, ﴿and to test the believers﴾, meaning: those firm in faith, ﴿from Him﴾, meaning: Him alone, ﴿with a good trial﴾, meaning: of victory, booty and reward. The root "bala'" (ب ل و), whether it is of the yā' or wāw type, in whatever arrangement, revolves around mixing. Sometimes it is absolute, as in "abla-hu 'udhran" (he gave him an excuse), and sometimes it is with multiplicity, effort and hardship, which is the most common state of this root. Sometimes it is for testing and sometimes for other than that. As for "mā ubālīhi bālah" (I do not care for him at all), I think it is from the "bāl" (mind/attention), which is the thought, so it is from "bawala" not "balawa," a hollow verb, not one of the four-radical type. Its meaning: I do not act toward him with my mind, i.e., I am not concerned with him; I do not turn my thought to mixing with his circumstances where he turns his thought to me; i.e., I do not think about his affair because of his insignificance to me. The meanings of this root will be expounded, Allah willing, in Surah Yusuf, peace be upon him, at His saying: ﴿What is the matter with the women?﴾ [Yusuf: 50]. And the meaning of this root is the opposite of ease (da'ah), because this one entails occupation of the mind, from which fatigue arises through repelling what clings to it, while ease entails calm of the inner self and emptiness of mind, which is the source of rest. So the meaning of the verse is that He, exalted be He, did this with the means of humiliating the disbelievers, so that there would mix with them of His affairs what would have an evil outcome for them in resisting it, and so that there would mix with the believers of that what would have a good outcome for them in undertaking it, indeed better than ease, because it leads them (p-245) to lasting rest, whereas ease leads to long fatigue. And Allah is the Granter of success.

When it was established by what has passed that He has great acts and mighty seizures, and the statements of those believers who said, "We were not prepared to meet the one with might," despite weakness of resolve, indicated this, He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, meaning: the One who encompasses all attributes of perfection, ﴿is All-Hearing﴾, meaning: of your statements, including seeking aid for help in victory and otherwise, ﴿All-Knowing﴾, meaning: of your resolutions, even if you do not speak them. So He rewards the believer according to his faith, and the disbeliever according to what he displays and conceals of his disbelief. The matter...

That: the one of great rank and far-reaching reach, who commanded you through His commands in it, forbade you through His prohibitions from His forbidden things, tested you in it with a fine trial, and showed you with your own eyes His weakening of this group that targeted you, while you were, in their sight, a morsel of camel meat and a sparrow between the claws of falcons. He also made clear to you some of the causes of that and the wonders of His power, leaving no excuse for a believer. So hold fast to His obedience, hasten to obey His Messenger, and do not look into the consequences of anything he commands. For he does not speak from desire; rather, it is only revelation from Us, and We have not commanded anything except after arranging it in the most judicious and perfect ways.

﴿And that﴾: i.e., and the matter is also that ﴿Allah﴾: i.e., the One comprising all the attributes of might and greatness ﴿weakens﴾: i.e., enfeebles, with a severe, firm, and everlasting enfeeblement, forever ﴿the plotting of the disbelievers﴾: i.e., those firmly rooted in disbelief, all of them. So do not be weak in pursuing the people. Even if a wound has touched you, We make it a purification for you and a destruction for the disbelievers, and the final outcome belongs to those who are mindful of God. We will inform you of their weaknesses, cast terror into their hearts, scatter their word, and undo what they have contrived. (p-246)

When this (the victory) entailed inflicting humiliation on the disbelievers through this encounter, and a promise that they would be compelled to suffer humiliation in the future, this was an elaboration of the *iltifāt* (a shift in mode of address, here from narration to direct address) toward threatening them in the form of mocking them and exalting the affair of the believers. So He said: ﴿If you seek a victory﴾, that is, ask for victory, O disbelievers, after this day, just as you sought victory in this encounter when you took hold of the curtains of the Ka'bah at the time of your departure, saying: "O God, give victory to the more guided of the two parties, the more noble of the two armies, the higher of the two groups, and the better of the two religions," and at the time the two hosts came in sight, by the words of Abu Jahl: "O God, whichever of us is more severed from kinship and has brought what is unknown, destroy him tomorrow." The victory has come to you, just as it came to you on this day. ﴿Then there has indeed come to you﴾, that is, on this day, with the victory of the believers, ﴿the victory﴾, that is, the one you sought, because they were the more guided of the two groups and the more noble of the two parties. ﴿And if you desist﴾, that is, after this, from such statements and actions that imply doubt or obstinacy, ﴿it is better for you﴾, and you have already seen the proofs of that. ﴿And if you return﴾, that is, to contending, since you have not desisted, ﴿We shall return﴾, that is, to forsaking you. ﴿And your company will not avail you﴾, that is, never, ﴿anything﴾, your group to which you turn for strength, ﴿[of any avail]﴾, that is, in terms of providing sufficiency, ﴿even if it is great in number﴾, because ﴿God is with the believers﴾... and the ﴿that God is﴾, that is, the Supreme King, ﴿with the believers﴾, that is, those firmly rooted in faith. Perhaps He used the future tense in the condition and the past tense in the consequent (p-247) to indicate that you sought victory at Badr and there came to you from the victory what you saw. So if it pleased you, then hold to it in the future, for I will never come to you, as long as you remain in your state, except with what I brought you on that day. The word "victory" may be understood in the sense of help, in which case it is mockery of them, or in the sense of judgment (qaḍā').

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 8, verse 20:

When the cause of what He inflicted upon the disbelievers (namely, His turning away from answering them in what they sought of their supplication, their being forsaken in this encounter, and the imposition of the like of that upon them forever) was their disobedience to the Messenger and their turning away from accepting what they heard from him of the Spirit, He warned the believers against the likes of their condition by persisting in disputing over the spoils of war or other matters. So He said: ﴿O you who believe﴾, i.e., who claim that, ﴿obey Allah﴾, i.e., the One to whom belongs all might and majesty, ﴿and His Messenger﴾, confirming your claim of faith.

And since obedience to the Messenger is obedience to Allah, because he only calls to Him, and his character is the Qur'an, He made the pronoun singular and said: ﴿and do not turn away from him﴾, i.e., from the Messenger, in any state, in any of the commands, whether concerning jihad or other matters, concerning the spoils or other things, whether it is light or heavy, easy or hard, ﴿while you hear﴾, i.e., while you have hearing for what he says, or, ﴿while you hear﴾ meaning while you accept it as true; for committing anything of that kind contradicts the claim of faith and resembles the condition of the disbelievers. And to this there is an allusion in His saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 8, verse 21:

﴿And do not be like those who say, "We hear,"﴾ that is, with their ears, ﴿while they do not hear.﴾ That is, they do not respond, so it is as if they had not heard. Since the fruit (thamarah) has been negated, that which bears fruit is considered non-existent.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 8, verse 22:

Since the state of those whose condition is this one resembled the state of the deaf in not hearing, because they derive no benefit from it, and the mute in not speaking, because they do not speak what benefits, and the one devoid of intellect (al-'adim lil-'aql) in not having intellect, because they derive no benefit from it, He said, giving the reason for this prohibition and expressing it with what is most suitable to what He described them with: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures﴾, i.e., those who crawl upon the face of the earth, placing them among the category of insects or beasts, then making them the worst of them.

Since they had those who surpass them, and the consideration is with what is with Him, glory be to Him, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿in the sight of Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses all perfection, including comprehensive knowledge, power and other attributes, ﴿are the deaf, the dumb﴾, i.e., the deaf in hearing and the mute in speech, the deafness and muteness being complete (bi-l-ghayn, i.e., with the ghayn, meaning intensified), ﴿who do not reason﴾, i.e., no intellect is renewed for them; and whoever does not benefit from hearing the caller is in this same state.

[p. 249] When that was the case, it might prompt the listener to say: "What is it with the Capable that He did not incline toward good those whose state is thus?" He answered that He had created them from the very beginning, and He may do in His dominion and kingdom whatever He wills, with a deep-rooted natural disposition (jibilla) toward corruption. He made their essences evil, like the essence of the scorpion, which accepts no discipline in any way and stings whatever it passes by. So He, glorified is He, knew that there was no good in them, and He left them to what He knew of them. ﴿If God had known﴾, that is, the One who possesses all perfection, ﴿any good in them﴾, that is, readiness to accept good, ﴿He would have made them hear﴾, that is, a hearing which is the true hearing, the kind that is followed by continuous response.

Since God's knowledge is all-encompassing, it must know everything that exists. Therefore, His not knowing that a thing exists entails that it does not exist. Accordingly, the implied sense here is: "But He did not know any good in them; rather, He knew that there was no good in them, so He did not grant them this hearing." ﴿And if He had made them hear﴾, while they were in this state of lacking readiness for good, a hearing by which He compelled them to respond, ﴿they would have turned away﴾, that is, after responding, ﴿while they were averse﴾, that is, their aversion would be firmly established, as they turned back on their heels. They would not have persisted in their response, because of their natural disposition to favor evil and shun good. So after turning toward Islam, they would have wanted nothing of Islam and its people except weakness. This is like the case of the apostates who were killed after having entered Islam out of fear of the sword and desire for wealth, and it belongs to the category of ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am 6:28].

God's knowledge has four categories: the totality of existing things; the totality of non-existing things; what each existing thing would be like if it were non-existent; and what each non-existing thing would be like if it were existent. The first two are knowledge of what actually is, and the last two are knowledge of what is decreed (qadar). This verse belongs to the last category. By my life, we have come to a time in which most people are, close to this matter, the boldest of people in falsehood, the most steadfast in pursuing it, the most expansive in the means of reaching it, the most cowardly when called to the truth, the swiftest to retreat when they are about to advance after effort, and the most tongue-tied when debating it. Thus what was supposed and hypothetical has become actual and existent.

The word "lau" (if/had) here may be the one by which one matter is made conditional upon another that is its opposite, so that the meaning is that the conditioned consequent is always present, like the saying of Umar, may God be pleased with him: "What a servant Suhayb is! Had he not feared God, he would not have disobeyed Him." Here the meaning on this reading is that if they turn away even with hearing and response, their turning away without these would be all the more so. This was pointed out by al-Razi. It may also be that it retains its original sense, that both clauses following it are negated. The negation of turning away is only good if it arises from the hearing that follows from knowing good in them. As for its absence because they were not made to hear the described hearing, since there is no good in them, that is not good in any way, but is pure evil. The negated turning away is not the turning away that is actually present in them, but the turning away that arises from the described hearing. Thus his claim does not contradict the realization of their obstinacy and their failure to submit. Its verification is that what is negated is only the increase of turning away arising from the hearing. The meaning is: "Had He made them hear, they would have increased in aversion," so what is negated in this context is that increase. And God is the Granter of success.

(p. 251) Since what preceded concerning the punishment of the disbelievers was caused by their failure to respond, He commanded the believers to respond, as a warning against being in the same situation as the disbelievers, lest they be gathered with them in their fate. So He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning: who have affirmed faith with their tongues. ﴿Respond﴾, meaning: make your claim true by actually responding, as one who is most eager for it. ﴿To Allah﴾, meaning: make this response exclusively for the One who possesses all the attributes of perfection. ﴿And to the Messenger﴾, the one He sent to all of creation.

Since he (ﷺ) was certainly calling them, because Allah the Exalted had commanded him to call them, and since he only called them to what Allah had commanded him, and since He, glorified is He, calls only to what is righteous and rightly guided, He used the particle of confirmation, made the pronoun singular, and stirred desire by mentioning the fruit of life, saying: ﴿when he calls you﴾, meaning: the Messenger, by urging and exhorting.

Since gathering the fruit of obedience is extremely near, He drew attention to this by using the preposition *li* (for) rather than *ila* (to), saying: ﴿to that which gives you life﴾, meaning: it will move you, through the honour of faith and knowledge, from the state of the disbelievers, with its deafness, muteness, and lack of reason, which is spiritual death, to spiritual life. And let nothing prevent you from responding in any matter by saying: "We have responded to faith and many of its laws," for had our Lord not known good in us He would not have made us hear, and so we are saved. Al-Bukhari in *al-Tafsir* and others narrated from Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I was praying when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by me and called me, but I did not come to him until I had finished the prayer. Then I came to him, and he said: 'What prevented you from coming?' I said: 'I was praying.' He said: 'Did not Allah say: ﴿O you who have believed, respond﴾ —' (p. 252) — the verse. Then he said: 'I will teach you the greatest surah in the Qur'an before I leave the mosque.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went to leave, and I reminded him, and he said: 'It is: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatiha: 2]. It is the seven oft-repeated and the great Qur'an which I have been given.'"

And al-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that "the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was praying, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Ubayy!' He turned, but did not answer him, and Ubayy continued praying and shortened it. Then he turned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'And upon you be peace. What prevented you, O Ubayy, from answering me when I called you?' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I was in prayer.' He said: 'Did you not find in what Allah revealed to me: ﴿Respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾?' He said: 'Yes! And I will not do it again, if Allah wills!' He said: 'Would you like me to teach you a surah that has not been sent down in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Furqan, the like of it?' He said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'How do you recite in prayer?' He recited *Umm al-Qur'an*, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, it has not been sent down in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Furqan, the like of it, and it is seven of the oft-repeated and the great Qur'an which I have been given.'" This is a hadith that is *hasan sahih*.
